issues.legal_issue: A conviction for murder may be upheld on circumstantial evidence when the established circumstances form a complete chain pointing to guilt and excluding reasonable possibilities consistent with innocence.
material_facts: The prosecution case rested on circumstantial evidence, with no eyewitness to the three killings.
The victims’ bodies were buried in a locked inner room of the premises where the accused and victims had lived; the room’s key was with one accused, and the room was accessible only to the accused.
Medical evidence established that the deaths were homicidal and that injuries had been inflicted with a sharp object found in the room.
The accused continued operating the business at the premises and did not seek to discover the whereabouts of the missing victims.
The courts found the established circumstances formed an unbroken chain consistent with the accused’s guilt.
issues.conclusion: The circumstantial evidence established the accused’s guilt, and their convictions for murder with common intention were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: In a case based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances forming the chain must be established and must be so complete as to rule out every reasonable possibility consistent with the accused’s innocence. Applying that principle, the Court relied on the proved circumstances as a whole to uphold the convictions under Sections 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

rule.if: circumstantial_evidence_appeal and complete_incriminating_chain and bodies_concealed_at_residence and accused_had_exclusive_access and homicidal_deaths_established

predicates.circumstantial_evidence_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction that rests on circumstantial evidence rather than eyewitness testimony.
predicates.complete_incriminating_chain: The established circumstances form an unbroken chain pointing to guilt and excluding reasonable possibilities consistent with innocence.
predicates.bodies_concealed_at_residence: The victims’ bodies were buried in an inner room of the premises where the accused lived.
predicates.accused_had_exclusive_access: The room where the bodies were buried was accessible only to the accused, and a key to it was in an accused’s possession.
predicates.homicidal_deaths_established: Medical evidence established that the victims died from injuries inflicted before death.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction based on circumstantial evidence and the established circumstances form a complete incriminating chain, including concealment of the victims at a residence under the accused’s exclusive access and proof of homicidal deaths, the conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: The death penalty is not warranted where the evidence does not establish that the murder falls within the rarest of rare cases calling for the extreme penalty.
material_facts: The appeal challenged death sentences imposed for the murders of three victims, including a young child.
The courts below relied on the cruelty of the killings, the fact that the child was not spared, and an asserted property motive as special reasons for imposing death.
The prosecution did not establish that the murders were cold-blooded, and the record did not show how they had occurred.
The Supreme Court concluded that the case did not fall within the rarest of rare category.
issues.conclusion: The death sentences were set aside and replaced with imprisonment for life, while the murder convictions were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 354(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, life imprisonment is the rule for murder and death is an exception requiring special reasons. Under Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab and Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab, death may be imposed only in rarest of rare cases; murders committed in an extremely brutal, grotesque, diabolical, revolting, or dastardly manner that arouse intense and extreme community indignation may fall within that category. The evidence here did not establish such a case.

predicates.death_sentence_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal reviewing a death sentence imposed for murder.
predicates.no_evidence_of_manner: The record does not establish how the murder was carried out.
predicates.no_proof_of_extreme_brutality: The prosecution has not proved circumstances establishing the extreme brutality required to place the murder in the rarest of rare category.

issues.definition: When an appeal reviews a death sentence and the record neither establishes how the murder was carried out nor proves the required extreme brutality, the death sentence is replaced with life imprisonment.
